name: Epidermal growth factor (EGF)
lead: Epidermal growth factor (EGF) is a small protein of 53 amino acids that stimulates cell growth, differentiation and survival by binding the EGF receptor (EGFR) on cell surfaces [1]. It was the second growth factor to be identified; Stanley Cohen found it while working with Rita Levi-Montalcini, and the two shared the 1986 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine [1].

In cosmetics, recombinant or synthetic EGF appears as an ingredient in some serums, where marketing describes it as supporting skin renewal and repair. In looksmaxxing and skincare discussion it is grouped with other growth-factor and peptide skincare ingredients.

Medically, a recombinant human EGF product (Heberprot-P) is used for diabetic foot ulcers, with evidence of improved healing described as tentative and safety described as poorly studied [1]. One small registered trial has examined an EGF facial serum for skin aging, with no published results found [2].

paras: EGF binds EGFR with high affinity and induces receptor dimerization, activating the receptor's tyrosine kinase and starting a signaling cascade that ultimately drives DNA synthesis and cell proliferation [1]. It occurs in platelets, urine, saliva, milk, tears and plasma [1]. Salivary EGF is reported to help maintain the integrity of oral, esophageal and gastric tissue [1].
EGF is the founding member of a protein family that includes HB-EGF, TGF-alpha and amphiregulin [1].
Recombinant human EGF sold as Heberprot-P can be injected into or applied to diabetic foot ulcers [1]. EGF is also used in research on bioengineered grafts and bone regeneration [1].
Skincare products listing EGF are sold as serums. Proponents say topical EGF promotes skin renewal, hydration and fine-line reduction. Published evidence for these cosmetic outcomes is sparse.

Because EGF signals through a pathway that promotes cell proliferation, researchers study the EGF pathway in cancer. Laboratory work has linked EGF to melanoma lymph node metastasis in a mouse model [3], and an EGF gene variant has been associated with esophageal adenocarcinoma risk [4]. These studies concern the biology of the pathway and not topical cosmetic products, and no study found has tested cancer risk from cosmetic EGF.

A registered trial (NCT05724589) evaluated an EGF serum for facial skin hydration, elasticity, pigmentation and wrinkles in 28 participants and is listed as completed; no results were available in the registry entry reviewed [2]. Larger trials of the EGFR-blocking antibody panitumumab (ABX-EGF) were cancer treatment studies and do not concern cosmetic EGF [5].

timeline.event: Cohen and Levi-Montalcini share the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for growth factor discoveries including EGF. [1]

lore.intro: EGF is discussed mainly as a skincare serum ingredient alongside peptides and growth factors; little looksmaxxing forum material exists to document.

claims.claim: Topical EGF serums rejuvenate skin and reduce wrinkles
claims.believers: Marketers and some users say EGF signals skin cells to renew, improving texture, hydration and fine lines.
claims.experts: One small registered trial of an EGF serum exists with no published results found [2]; the Wikipedia article on EGF does not describe cosmetic evidence [1].

claims.claim: EGF is a safe skincare ingredient because it is a natural protein
claims.believers: Users point to EGF occurring naturally in saliva and tears.
claims.experts: EGF signaling is a research focus in cancer biology [3][4], and safety of medical EGF treatment is described as poorly studied [1]; no published study found has tested cancer risk from cosmetic use.

card.summary: A growth-factor protein sold in skincare serums; real biology, one tiny serum trial with no published results.
card.note: EGF signaling is studied in cancer biology; cosmetic safety is untested.

quick.overview:
Epidermal growth factor is a natural protein that tells cells to grow and divide. Its discoverers won a Nobel Prize, and it appears in some cosmetic serums.

A recombinant form is used for diabetic foot ulcers. For skin appearance, only one small registered serum trial was found, with no published results.
quick.mechanism: EGF binds its receptor EGFR on cells, triggering signaling that drives proliferation and survival.
quick.risks: Safety of medical EGF is described as poorly studied, and EGF signaling is a research focus in cancers. No study found has tested cosmetic EGF for cancer risk.
